newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - flat, Harris Cty reprices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - flat, Harris Cty reprices.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were flat to slightly lower in quiet trading Monday, as players geared up for the week's heavy supply.
The secondary market saw only a few small bid-wanted lists and only a handful of trades the entire day, one trader said.
"Everyone's going to sit and wait and see where the scales are" on the week's coming new issues, the trader said, adding that the tone Monday was "heavy" given slippage in Treasuries.
The government long bond was off 8/32 at 98-29/32 to yield 6.84 percent heading into the New York close.
In the muni secondary, bids on Cook County, Ill., FGIC 5-7/8s of 2022 were bid at a 5.99 percent yield, up one basis point from Friday.
Intermountain Power Agency, Utah, 5.0s of 2021 were three basis points higher, at 5.89 percent, slipping further from a one basis point rise at midday.

Goldman Sachs & Co repriced $239 million Harris County, Texas, general obligation bonds late in the afternoon, raising yields in many maturities and lifting the 2023 maturity to 5.85 percent from 5.82 percent.

Tuesday is expected to feature at least $1.1 billion of negotiated issues, topped by a $447.5 million North Carolina Eastern Municipal Power Agency deal, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Forty-two deals totaling $485 million are on the Reuters competitive calendar for Tuesday, including a $38.5 million Wisconsin issue at 1100 EDT.
The largest competitive deal of the week comes Wednesday with the Virginia Public School Authority's $133 million issue.

The rest of the week is expected to feature several other large negotiated issues, including $775 million taxable New York State Dormitory Authority bonds through senior manager Lehman Brothers and nearly $600 million N.Y. Urban Development Corp bonds through PaineWebber Inc.
Tuesday data releases include the Employment Cost Index for the third quarter.

Elsewhere, the closely watched October employment report is expected on Friday. Economists polled by Reuters expect on average that the non-farm payrolls figure will show a 212,000 increase and the unemployment rate will hold steady at 5.2 percent.
